chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
"When you eat, recline on your back and place your right leg over your left."

key_terms.قَفَاكَ: your back (specifically the back of the neck/upper back)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended posture for eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him), recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, prescribes a specific posture for eating—reclining on the back with the right leg over the left—which reflects the Prophetic tradition of physical ease during meals. While often discussed alongside general adab (etiquette), this specific instruction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on bodily comfort and moderation as part of spiritual discipline. The practice is viewed not merely as a physical habit but as a means to facilitate digestion and maintain mindfulness during consumption.
